questions.text:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. The Revolt of 1857 began at Meerut on 10 May 1857.
2. Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi was one of its leaders.
3. It was led at Kanpur by Kunwar Singh.
questions.explanation: At Kanpur the revolt was led by Nana Sahib; Kunwar Singh led it in Bihar.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Leaders of 1857.
Options A, B and D are out: 2 statement(s) are correct, not this number.
Common slip to avoid: Linking Kunwar Singh with Kanpur.
So the answer is option C: Only two.

questions.text: Which was the first Indian state annexed by Lord Dalhousie under the Doctrine of Lapse?
questions.explanation: Satara was annexed in 1848, the first state taken under the Doctrine of Lapse.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Doctrine of Lapse.
Options A and C are out: Annexed in 1854.
Option D (Awadh) is out: Annexed in 1856 on the charge of misgovernment.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing the better-known Jhansi.
So the answer is option B: Satara.
wrongReasons: Annexed in 1856 on the charge of misgovernment

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about the inscriptions of Ashoka.
1. They were first deciphered by James Prinsep.
2. Major Rock Edict XIII describes the Kalinga war.
3. They are written only in the Brahmi script.
questions.explanation: Some edicts are in Kharosthi, Greek and Aramaic as well.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Ashokan inscriptions.
Options A and C are out: Includes statement 3, which is incorrect.
Option D (1, 2 and 3) is out: Statement 3 is incorrect.
Common slip to avoid: Assuming one script for all edicts.
So the answer is option B: 1 and 2 only.
questions.trap: Assuming one script for all edicts.

questions.text:
Assertion (A): The Rajya Sabha cannot reject a Money Bill.
Reason (R): It can only recommend amendments to a Money Bill, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Under Article 109 the Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill within 14 days; its recommendations are not binding, so it cannot block the Bill.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Article 109.
Options A, C and D are out: Does not match the truth of A and R.
Common slip to avoid: Treating the Rajya Sabha as equal to the Lok Sabha on money matters.
So the answer is option B: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.trap: Treating the Rajya Sabha as equal to the Lok Sabha on money matters.
wrongReasons: Does not match the truth of A and R
Does not match the truth of A and R
Does not match the truth of A and R

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about Fundamental Duties.
1. They were added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.
2. They were added on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
3. They can be enforced by courts through writs.
questions.explanation: Fundamental Duties are not justiciable and cannot be enforced through writs.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Part IVA.
Options A and B are out: Includes statement 3, which is incorrect.
Option C (1, 2 and 3) is out: Statement 3 is incorrect.
Common slip to avoid: Treating them like Fundamental Rights.
So the answer is option D: 1 and 2 only.

questions.text: The Right to Education was made a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years by which Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 86th Amendment inserted Article 21A.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Article 21A.
Option B (42nd Amendment, 1976) is out: Added Fundamental Duties.
Option C (44th Amendment, 1978) is out: Removed the right to property from Part III.
Option D (73rd Amendment, 1992) is out: Gave constitutional status to Panchayats.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing the 42nd.
So the answer is option A: 86th Amendment, 2002.
wrongReasons: Removed the right to property from Part III

questions.text:

2. The Cash Reserve Ratio is the share of deposits that banks must keep with the RBI.
3. The Statutory Liquidity Ratio must be maintained entirely as cash with the RBI.
questions.explanation: SLR is held by banks themselves in cash, gold or approved securities, not with the RBI.
steps: Spot what the question tests: CRR vs SLR.
Options A, B and C are out: 2 statement(s) are correct, not this number.
Common slip to avoid: Mixing up CRR and SLR.
So the answer is option D: Only two.

questions.text: Which Five-Year Plan was based on the Mahalanobis model, which stressed rapid growth of heavy industries?
questions.explanation: The Second Plan (1956-61) followed the Mahalanobis model.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Planning models.
Option B (First Plan) is out: Based on the Harrod-Domar model.
Option C (Third Plan) is out: Called a 'take-off' plan for self-reliance.
Option D (Fifth Plan) is out: Stressed 'Garibi Hatao'.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing the First Plan.
So the answer is option A: Second Plan.

questions.text: Which of the following is a capital receipt of the Government of India?
options: Recovery of loans granted to States
questions.explanation: Recovery of loans reduces an asset of the government and is a capital receipt.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Revenue and capital receipts.
Option A (Corporation tax) is out: A tax revenue.
Options C and D are out: A non-tax revenue.
Common slip to avoid: Treating interest as a capital receipt.
So the answer is option B: Recovery of loans granted to States.
questions.trap: Treating interest as a capital receipt.

questions.text: Through how many Indian States does the Tropic of Cancer pass?
questions.explanation: It passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Tropic of Cancer.
Option A (7) is out: One fewer.
Option B (9) is out: One more.
Option D (6) is out: Two fewer.
Common slip to avoid: Forgetting Tripura or Mizoram.
So the answer is option C: 8.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about the climate of India.
1. Western Disturbances bring winter rainfall to north-western India.
2. El Nino years are generally associated with a weaker south-west monsoon.
3. The leeward side of the Western Ghats receives more rainfall than the windward side.
questions.explanation: The windward side receives heavy rainfall; the leeward side lies in the rain shadow.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Monsoon and rain shadow.
Options A and C are out: Includes statement 3, which is incorrect.
Option D (1, 2 and 3) is out: Statement 3 is incorrect.
Common slip to avoid: Reversing windward and leeward.
So the answer is option B: 1 and 2 only.

questions.text: Which channel separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands?
questions.explanation: The Ten Degree Channel lies along 10 degrees north between the two groups.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Channels and passages.
Option A (Palk Strait) is out: Separates India from Sri Lanka.
Option B (Eight Degree Channel) is out: Separates Minicoy from the Maldives.
Option D (Duncan Passage) is out: Separates South Andaman from Little Andaman.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing Duncan Passage.
So the answer is option C: Ten Degree Channel.
wrongReasons: Separates South Andaman from Little Andaman

questions.text: Which blood group is called the universal recipient?
questions.explanation: AB positive blood has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies and has the Rh factor.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Blood groups.
Option B (O negative) is out: The universal donor.
Option C (A positive) is out: Lacks the B antigen.
Option D (B negative) is out: Lacks the A antigen.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing the universal donor.
So the answer is option A: AB positive.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about lenses.
1. A concave lens always forms a virtual image of a real object.
2. The power of a lens in dioptres is the reciprocal of its focal length in metres.
3. Myopia is corrected by a convex lens.
questions.explanation: Myopia is corrected by a concave lens; hypermetropia by a convex lens.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Lenses and defects of vision.
Options A and B are out: Includes statement 3, which is incorrect.
Option C (1, 2 and 3) is out: Statement 3 is incorrect.
Common slip to avoid: Swapping the lenses.
So the answer is option D: 1 and 2 only.

questions.text:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.
2. Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin.
3. Solder is an alloy of lead and tin.
questions.explanation: All three alloys are made of the metals stated.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Common alloys.
Options A, B and D are out: 3 statement(s) are correct, not this number.

questions.text:
Match List I (Dance) with List II (State of origin).
A. Kuchipudi  B. Mohiniyattam  C. Sattriya  D. Bharatanatyam.
1. Assam  2. Kerala  3. Andhra Pradesh  4. Tamil Nadu
questions.explanation: Kuchipudi is from Andhra Pradesh, Mohiniyattam from Kerala, Sattriya from Assam and Bharatanatyam from Tamil Nadu.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Classical dances.
Option A (A-2, B-3, C-1, D-4) is out: Kuchipudi and Mohiniyattam are swapped.
Option B (A-3, B-1, C-2, D-4) is out: Mohiniyattam and Sattriya are swapped.
Option D (A-3, B-2, C-4, D-1) is out: Sattriya and Bharatanatyam are swapped.
Common slip to avoid: Mixing southern dances.
So the answer is option C: A-3, B-2, C-1, D-4.

questions.text: In 2021 the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna was renamed in honour of which hockey legend?
questions.explanation: The award is now the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Sports awards.
Options A and B are out: Not the namesake.
Option C (Milkha Singh) is out: A sprinter, not a hockey player.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing another hockey name.
So the answer is option D: Major Dhyan Chand.
wrongReasons: A sprinter, not a hockey player

How many of the following statements about the Assembly elections of May 2026 are correct?

questions.text: The 30th UN Climate Change Conference (COP30), held in November 2025 at Belem, was hosted by which country?
questions.explanation: COP30 was held at Belem, on the edge of the Amazon, in Brazil.
steps: Spot what the question tests: COP summits.
Options B and C are out: Not the host.
Option D (Azerbaijan) is out: Hosted COP29 in 2024.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing the previous host.
So the answer is option A: Brazil.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about Operation Sindoor.
1. It followed the terror attack at Pahalgam on 22 April 2025.
2. It was launched on 7 May 2025.
3. It was carried out by the Indian Army alone.
questions.explanation: The operation involved all three services: the Army, the Navy and the Air Force.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Operation Sindoor.
Options A and C are out: Includes statement 3, which is incorrect.
Option D (1, 2 and 3) is out: Statement 3 is incorrect.
Common slip to avoid: Assuming a single service.
So the answer is option B: 1 and 2 only.

questions.text: The 26th SCO summit was held in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, in 2026. Which country took over the rotating SCO chairmanship?
questions.explanation: The summit was held on 31 August to 1 September 2026, marking SCO's 25th anniversary. Pakistan took over the chair; Modi called for action against terrorism.
steps: Spot what the question tests: SCO summit 2026.
Option B (India) is out: It chaired in 2022-23.
Option C (Kazakhstan) is out: It chaired in 2023-24.
Option D (China) is out: It chaired in 2024-25.
Common slip to avoid: Picking a recent former chair.
So the answer is option A: Pakistan.

questions.text: In September 2026 Dhiraj Bommadevara became the first Indian man to win the recurve gold at which competition?
questions.explanation: He won the Archery World Cup Final in Saltillo, Mexico, beating Japan's Nakanishi Junya in a shoot-off.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Archery 2026.
Option B (Olympic Games) is out: Not the event of his September 2026 win.
Option C (World Archery Championships) is out: Not the event of his September 2026 win.
Option D (Asian Games) is out: Not the event of his September 2026 win.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing a bigger-sounding event.
So the answer is option A: Archery World Cup Final.

questions.text: The 2026 G7 summit, attended by PM Modi in June as an outreach guest, was held at Evian in which country?
questions.explanation: France hosted the 2026 G7 summit at Evian, mid-June. India is not a G7 member but is a regular outreach invitee.
steps: Spot what the question tests: G7 2026.
Option A (Italy) is out: Hosted the 2024 summit.
Option B (Canada) is out: Hosted the 2025 summit.
Option C (Germany) is out: Not the 2026 host.
Common slip to avoid: Confusing recent hosts.
So the answer is option D: France.

questions.text: At the 71st National Film Awards in September 2025, the Dadasaheb Phalke Award was conferred on which actor?
questions.explanation: President Droupadi Murmu presented the award to Mohanlal.
steps: Spot what the question tests: Dadasaheb Phalke Award.
Option A (Mammootty) is out: Not the recipient.
Option B (Rajinikanth) is out: Received it for 2019.
Option C (Amitabh Bachchan) is out: Received it for 2018.
Common slip to avoid: Choosing an earlier recipient.
So the answer is option D: Mohanlal.

questions.text: In June 2026 economist Neelkanth Mishra was appointed India's Executive Director at which institution?
questions.explanation: Mishra was appointed India's Executive Director at the World Bank for three years, succeeding Parameswaran Iyer.
steps: Spot what the question tests: World Bank.
Option B (International Monetary Fund) is out: India has a separate post there.
Option C (Asian Development Bank) is out: Not this appointment.
Option D (New Development Bank) is out: Not this appointment.
Common slip to avoid: Confusing the Bretton Woods institutions.
So the answer is option A: World Bank.
wrongReasons: India has a separate post there
